body:
### Summary

When several `uvx` invocations of the same tool start at the same time against a cold cache, each one builds its own cached environment under `archive-v0`. Only one of them ends up referenced from `environments-v2`; the others are orphaned and are never reused, so they stay on disk until someone runs `uv cache prune`.

This is easy to hit with MCP servers, because agent apps (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI and others) launch the same `uvx <server>` command once per open session, often several at once.

### Reproduction (uv 0.13.7, macOS arm64)

```sh
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do uvx pycowsay --help >/dev/null 2>&1 & done; wait
find "$UV_CACHE_DIR/archive-v0" -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -name pyvenv.cfg | wc -l   # 8
ls "$UV_CACHE_DIR/environments-v2" | wc -l                                         # 1

# sequential runs afterwards reuse one of them and never touch the other 7
for i in 1 2 3; do uvx pycowsay --help >/dev/null 2>&1; done
find "$UV_CACHE_DIR/archive-v0" -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -name pyvenv.cfg | wc -l   # still 8
```

Control: three sequential runs against a fresh cache produce 1 environment, as expected. I reproduced the same result twice with `mcp-proxy-for-aws@1.6.4` and with `httpie`, on 0.13.7 and on 0.12.13.

### Expected

Concurrent invocations that resolve to the same environment should end up sharing one cached environment (for example by taking a lock on the environment key while it is being built, similar to what was suggested in #17399), or at least the losers of the race should remove the environment they built.

### Real-world impact, and a related question

On my machine `~/.cache/uv` reached about 235 GB, which filled the disk. Almost all of it was 1,323 cached tool environments in `archive-v0` (about 202 GB by `du`), created by six `uvx`-launched MCP servers over roughly two months:

- 157 of them (about 20 GB) are exact duplicates: same uv version, same interpreter, identical installed package set. 32 identical environments for `mcp-proxy-for-aws==1.6.4` were all created within the same minute, which is the race above.
- The other 1,166 are distinct, because the tool or one of its dependencies released a new version (for example `botocore`, which publishes almost daily), so each new resolution produced a new environment. The superseded ones are never removed either.

The second part is expected behaviour as far as I can tell (and overlaps with #5731, #9790 and #13431), but it suggests a narrower improvement than a general cache size limit: when `uvx` creates a new environment for a tool whose previous environment has been superseded, the old one could be dropped automatically. For long-running, frequently relaunched tools like MCP servers, the cache otherwise grows without bound and users usually only find out when the disk is full. `uv cache prune` does clean all of this up correctly, which is great; the problem is that nothing prompts people to run it.

Thank you for uv, and for considering this.

### Platform

macOS 26.6 (arm64)

### Version

uv 0.13.7 (316c827e0 2026-11-03 aarch64-apple-darwin); also seen on 0.12.13 (Homebrew)

### Python version

Python 3.14.7 (uv-managed)
title: Concurrent uvx runs on a cold cache each build their own environment, orphaning all but one
